sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜总会打碟的时候，每天晚上你要带着 300 件你最珍贵的传家宝去工作，你把一个DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个美丽的、有50年历史的文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在您最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Caitlin Dickerson.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是凯特琳·迪克森。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, in the aftermath of 9-11, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，在9·11事件之后，美国

sentences.en: government developed a new set of interrogation techniques to be used on terror suspects in secret prisons around the world.
sentences.zh: 政府开发了一套新的审讯技术，用于世界各地秘密监狱中的恐怖主义嫌疑人。

sentences.en: The result was a CIA torture program so brutal it was later abolished.
sentences.zh: 其结果是一个极其残酷的中央情报局酷刑计划，后来被废除了。

sentences.en: But until now, no one has been held accountable.
sentences.zh: 但直到现在，还没有人被追究责任。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月21日，星期三。

sentences.en: Mr. Saleem.
sentences.zh: 萨利姆先生。

sentences.en: Do you know what a flashback is?
sentences.zh: 你知道什么是闪回吗？

sentences.en: What does your flashback mean?
sentences.zh: 你的闪回意味着什么？

sentences.en: Flashback?
sentences.zh: 闪回？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: What does your flashback mean?
sentences.zh: 你的闪回意味着什么？

sentences.en: Like, thinking of something that happened before.
sentences.zh: 就像，想起以前发生的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Do you experience flashbacks?
sentences.zh: 你有过闪回的经历吗？

sentences.en: Well, but there's a flashback.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是有一种闪回。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And what do you flashback to?
sentences.zh: 那你闪回到什么？

sentences.en: Most of the time, one thing.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，是一件事。

sentences.en: And what is that, then?
sentences.zh: 那是什么呢？

sentences.en: Okay, sir.
sentences.zh: 好的，先生。

sentences.en: Tortured.
sentences.zh: 受虐待。

sentences.en: Being tortured.
sentences.zh: 遭受虐待。

sentences.en: Between 2002 and 2008, the CIA has acknowledged that at least 39 men were subjected to enhanced interrogation techniques in their secret prisons.
sentences.zh: 中央情报局承认，在2002年至2008年期间，至少有39名男子在其秘密监狱中遭受了强化审讯技术。

sentences.en: One of them, Ghul Rachman, died as a result.
sentences.zh: 其中一人古尔·拉赫曼因此死亡。

sentences.en: Now, that victim's family and two others who were interrogated are plaintiffs in a civil suit.
sentences.zh: 现在，受害者的家属和另外两名受审讯的人是民事诉讼的原告。

sentences.en: Not against the CIA, which is protected.
sentences.zh: 不是针对受到保护的中情局。

sentences.en: Instead, they're targeting two government contractors, psychologists.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们的目标是两个政府承包商，心理学家。

sentences.en: Mr. Suter, are you saying that everything that happened to you while you were at Cobalt was part of the program that was designed by Drs.
sentences.zh: 苏特先生，你是说你在科巴特时发生在你身上的所有事情，都是由

sentences.en: Mitchell and Jessen?
sentences.zh: 米切尔和杰森博士设计的计划的一部分吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Michael spoke with our colleague Sherry Fink about the role of these psychologists in the program.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔与我们的同事谢莉·芬克讨论了这些心理学家在计划中的角色。

sentences.en: You know, I know it's easy and glib to say that if someone who is the expert on al-Qaeda just told you they're getting ready to set off a nuclear bomb,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人说基地组织的专家刚刚告诉你他们准备引爆一枚核弹，说这话很容易也很轻率，

sentences.en: that you can say, no, no, hands off, I don't want to participate.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，不，不，别插手，我不想参与。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the way it was for me.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说情况并非如此。

sentences.en: I was willing to help.
sentences.zh: 我愿意帮忙。

sentences.en: If what happened as a result of that that was that I couldn't go back to doing marital therapy, I was okay with that.
sentences.zh: 如果因此导致的结果是我不能回去做婚姻治疗，我对此没有意见。

sentences.en: Who are James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen?
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·米切尔和布鲁斯·杰森是谁？

sentences.en: James Mitchell and Bruce Jessen are psychologists.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·米切尔和布鲁斯·杰森是心理学家。

sentences.en: I have a four-year degree in psychology.
sentences.zh: 我有一个四年制的心理学学位。

sentences.en: They're retired military psychologists.
sentences.zh: 他们是退休的军事心理学家。

sentences.en: I have a master's degree in psychology from the University of Alaska in Anchorage.
sentences.zh: 我拥有安克雷奇阿拉斯加大学的心理学硕士学位。

sentences.en: When they were in the military, they ran and were very involved in so-called SEER training.
sentences.zh: 当他们在军队时，他们负责并深度参与了所谓的SEER训练。

sentences.en: And just so the record is clear,
sentences.zh: 为了记录清楚，

sentences.en: SEER stands for survival, evasion, resistance, and escape.
sentences.zh: SEER代表生存、逃避、抵抗和逃脱。

sentences.en: The resolve of our great nation...
sentences.zh: 我们伟大的国家的决心……

sentences.en: After 9-11...
...is being tested.
sentences.zh: ……正在受到考验。

sentences.en: There was a sense in America that there could be another attack at any time.
sentences.zh: 美国有一种感觉，随时可能发生另一次袭击。

sentences.en: But make no mistake.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问。

sentences.en: We will show the world that we will pass this teSt.
sentences.zh: 我们将向世界展示，我们将通过这场测试。

sentences.en: There was this sense of we need to get information from them, suspected terrorists, before the next attack.
sentences.zh: 有一种我们需要从他们那里获取信息的感觉，即嫌疑恐怖分子，在下一次袭击之前。

sentences.en: I believe I took the...
sentences.zh: 我相信我拿了……

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I don't believe.
sentences.zh: 我不相信。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I took the appropriate actions as the commander in chief.
sentences.zh: 作为总司令，我采取了适当的行动。

sentences.en: And so the CIA turned to James Mitchell.
sentences.zh: 所以中情局求助于詹姆斯·米切尔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: James Mitchell got his colleague, Bruce Jessen, involved.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·米切尔让他的同事布鲁斯·杰森参与进来。

sentences.en: And that's what initiated me being called.
sentences.zh: 这就是我被叫到的原因。

sentences.en: They became CIA contractors to get involved with questioning suspects, terrorism suspects in the war on terror.
sentences.zh: 他们成为了中情局的承包商，参与在反恐战争中审问嫌疑人，恐怖主义嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Jim and I went into a cubicle.
sentences.zh: 吉姆和我进了一个小隔间。

sentences.en: They literally tapped it out on a typewriter, a proposal for 12 EITs, enhanced interrogation techniques, that our military was using in its training programs
sentences.zh: 他们真的用打字机敲打出了一份关于12种EIT（强化审讯技术）的提案，这些技术是我们的军队在其训练项目中使用的

sentences.en: to help our soldiers resist interrogation so that you could kind of reverse engineer those techniques and apply them in the interrogation of actual terrorism suspects.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助我们的士兵抵抗审讯，这样你就可以对这些技术进行某种逆向工程，并将它们应用对实际恐怖主义嫌疑人的审讯中。

sentences.en: We provided them with a liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们给他们提供了一份名单。

sentences.en: We didn't develop a bunch of new EITs.
sentences.zh: 我们没有开发出一堆新的EIT。

sentences.en: Everything from waterboarding, which is like a simulated drowning, to putting men into small boxes, to sleep deprivation techniques, so-called walling.
sentences.zh: 从水刑（类似于模拟溺水），到把人关进小盒子，再到睡眠剥夺技术，所谓的撞墙。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I thought walling was effective.
sentences.zh: 我认为撞墙是有效的。

sentences.en: Men are like slammed against a flexible plywood wall, which creates a terrifying sound.
sentences.zh: 人们被猛烈撞击在灵活的胶合板墙上，这会产生可怕的声音。

sentences.en: It jostles at the inner ear.
sentences.zh: 它震动了内耳。

sentences.en: It makes a really loud noise.
sentences.zh: 它发出了非常大的声音。

sentences.en: It sounds pretty tremendous.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常震撼。

sentences.en: So these were the techniques that they tapped up on this typewriter.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是他们在打字机上敲出来的技术。

sentences.en: And of these, which my question was, which ones did they not adopt?
sentences.zh: 在这些中，我的问题是，他们没有采用哪一个？

sentences.en: It would be a shorter list than the ones that they did.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个比他们采用的更短的清单。

sentences.en: I don't think they did.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们做到了。

sentences.en: They didn't do mock burial.
sentences.zh: 他们没有做模拟葬礼。

sentences.en: I think that's the only one.
sentences.zh: 我想那是唯一的一个。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: I don't recall insects either.
sentences.zh: 我也不记得有昆虫。

sentences.en: Insects.
sentences.zh: 昆虫。

sentences.en: Yeah, the use of insects to terrify the men.
sentences.zh: 是的，利用昆虫来吓唬人。

sentences.en: And did these two men's involvement stop at typing out, developing this list of techniques?
sentences.zh: 这两个人的参与是否止步于打字、开发这份技术清单？

sentences.en: No, it didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，并非如此。

sentences.en: They were then asked to actually apply the techniques.
sentences.zh: 然后他们被要求实际应用这些技术。

sentences.en: The worry and intensity had reached a peak because the CIA had been sorely chastised and felt culpable about 9-11.
sentences.zh: 担忧和紧张情绪达到了顶峰，因为中情局受到了严厉的训斥，对9·11事件感到负有罪责。

sentences.en: Abu Zubaydah was the first suspect with whom they worked and waterboarded multiple times.
sentences.zh: 阿布·祖巴达是他们合作并多次进行水刑的第一个嫌疑人。

sentences.en: This was a suspect who the CIA felt like they just weren't getting enough out of, that they felt like maybe he's got some really important information,
sentences.zh: 这是一个中情局觉得他们没有从中榨取足够信息的嫌疑人，他们觉得也许他掌握了一些非常重要的信息，

sentences.en: and it could stop another attack.
sentences.zh: 这可以阻止另一场袭击。

sentences.en: Now, I think we know now that generally, once you've held somebody for a period of time, the immediate usefulness of their information is going to go down.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想我们现在知道，一般来说，一旦你关押一个人一段时间，他们信息的即时效用就会下降。

sentences.en: But at the time, if we're to believe what the CIA has said, there was some sense of urgency around his interrogation.
sentences.zh: 但当时，如果我们相信中情局所说的话，他的审讯周围有一种紧迫感。

sentences.en: And so Mitchell and Jessen are sent out and they begin working with his interrogation.
sentences.zh: 所以米切尔和杰森被派去，他们开始参与他的审讯。

sentences.en: But I've been in the military my whole life and was committed to and used to doing what I was ordered to do.
sentences.zh: 但我一生都在军队，致力于并习惯于做我被命令去做的事情。

sentences.en: That's the way I considered this circumstance, and so I went.
sentences.zh: 这就是我看待这种情况的方式，所以我去了。

sentences.en: And they started to apply the techniques.
sentences.zh: 他们开始应用这些技术。

sentences.en: Themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己。

sentences.en: Themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己。

sentences.en: Had you ever actually performed any intelligence-gathering interrogations before this?
sentences.zh: 在此之前你实际执行过任何情报搜集审讯吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Well, they waterboarded him multiple times over a period of a couple weeks.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在几周的时间里，他们对他进行了多次水刑。

sentences.en: But still, I was thinking that I wasn't going to be the guy doing it.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我还是认为我不会是那个动手的人。

sentences.en: I thought it could be done safely.
sentences.zh: 我以为这可以安全地完成。

sentences.en: I thought he would be uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 我以为他会不舒服。

sentences.en: It sucks.
sentences.zh: 这很糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know that it's painful.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道这是否痛苦。

sentences.en: I saw an interview.
sentences.zh: 我看到过一个采访。

sentences.en: But it's distressing.
sentences.zh: 但这令人痛苦。

sentences.en: You're there to prevent, in this case, a catastrophic nuclear attack against your own country.
sentences.zh: 你在那里是为了防止，在这种情况下，对你自己的国家的灾难性核袭击。

sentences.en: Your wife, your children, your grandparents.
sentences.zh: 你的妻子，你的孩子，你的祖父母。

sentences.en: You, if I may emphasize a little bit.
sentences.zh: 如果你允许我稍微强调一下。

sentences.en: If I want to get information from you, Dor.
sentences.zh: 如果我想从你那里得到情报，多尔。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: If I want to get information from you, Dor,
sentences.zh: 如果我想从你那里得到情报，多尔，

sentences.en: I don't want to slap you.
sentences.zh: 我不想扇你耳光。

sentences.en: I don't want to wall you.
sentences.zh: 我不想撞你的墙。

sentences.en: I don't want to waterboard you.
sentences.zh: 我不想对你施水刑。

sentences.en: Even if you're my enemy, who we believe has information that's going to devastate our country,
sentences.zh: 即使你是我们的敌人，我们认为你掌握了将毁灭我们国家的信息，

sentences.en: we want you to cooperate.
sentences.zh: 我们希望你合作。

sentences.en: We know that you're a soldier of some type.
sentences.zh: 我们知道你是某种军人。

sentences.en: You're a terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 你是个恐怖分子。

sentences.en: But these men were like Jedi Knights.
sentences.zh: 但这些人就像绝地武士。

sentences.en: These men that we worked on were utterly and totally committed.
sentences.zh: 我们合作的这些人是完全且绝对投入的。

sentences.en: They had the faith that most people of faith wish they had.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有大多数有信仰的人希望拥有的信念。

sentences.en: Unwaverable.
sentences.zh: 坚定不移。

sentences.en: So after waterboarding Abu Zubaydah several times, at some point they say that they realized that there was no utility to continuing.
sentences.zh: 所以在对阿布·祖巴达进行多次水刑后，他们在某个时候说他们意识到继续下去没有任何用处。

sentences.en: And so their recommendation back to CIA headquarters was, let's stop.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们向中情局总部的建议是，停下来。

sentences.en: What was the response from the CIA when they asked to stop?
sentences.zh: 当中情局被要求停下来时，他们的反应是什么？

sentences.en: What they said was, well, you guys have lost your spine.
sentences.zh: 他们说的是，你们这些家伙失去了骨气。

sentences.en: I think the word that was actually used is that you guys are pussies.
sentences.zh: 我想实际使用的词是你们这些家伙是懦夫。

sentences.en: There's going to be another attack in America, and the blood of dead civilians are going to be on your hands.
sentences.zh: 美国将发生另一次袭击，平民死亡的鲜血将沾满你们的手。

sentences.en: If you won't follow through with this, then we're going to send somebody out there who will.
sentences.zh: 如果你不坚持到底，那么我们将派一个会这样做的人去。

sentences.en: We even talked to Zubaydah about if he had any ideas, what we could do besides that.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至和祖巴达谈过，看他有什么主意，除了那个我们还能做什么。

sentences.en: And as you probably know, he cautioned us not to stop using it because of various reasons that I don't need to state now.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的，他告诫我们不要停止使用它，原因有很多，我现在不需要说明。

sentences.en: And he alleges that Abu Zubaydah said, no, keep using the waterboard because only that will allow the other terrorism suspects to actually give you information.
sentences.zh: 他声称阿布·祖巴达说，不，继续使用水刑，因为只有这样才能让其他恐怖主义嫌疑人真正向你提供信息。

sentences.en: Like if they're actually being subjected to something that extreme, then that would be the only way that they could cooperate with you.
sentences.zh: 就像如果他们真的经受了那样极端的事情，那将是他们能够与你合作的唯一方式。

sentences.en: Now, we don't have Abu Zubaydah's side of that because he's still in Guantanamo.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们没有阿布·祖巴达方面的说法，因为他仍在关塔那摩。

sentences.en: You know, we're depending on the psychologists for that version of the event.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们依靠心理学家来了解那一事件的版本。

sentences.en: But it was pretty shocking.
sentences.zh: 但这相当令人震惊。

sentences.en: Well, right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pretty – it has to be unusual for interrogators to ask the person they're interrogating how to interrogate them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，审讯人员反过来向被审讯的人请教该怎么审讯，这在当时肯定是极不寻常的。

sentences.en: What does that tell you, if anything?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么，如果有的话？

sentences.en: They didn't have experience interrogating terrorism suspects.
sentences.zh: 他们缺乏审讯恐怖主义嫌疑人的经验。

sentences.en: So it is quite notable that they would go so far as to ask one of the people they were interrogating for, you know, feedback on their techniques.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们竟然会向被审讯的对象征求对其审讯手法的反馈，这相当引人注目。

sentences.en: That is a bit shocking.
sentences.zh: 这确实有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: And also maybe suggest some level of self-doubt, maybe.
sentences.zh: 而且也许在某种程度上表明了一种自我怀疑，或许吧。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: But they certainly spoke – really for the first time that I've heard, you get the sense of a man, particularly with Dr. Jessen, wrestling with this.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实敞开了心扉——据我所知这还是头一次，你能感受到一个人，尤其是杰森博士，在内心的挣扎。

sentences.en: I think any normal, conscionable man would have to consider carefully doing something like this.
sentences.zh: 我想任何一个有良知的正常人，在做这种事时都必须谨慎考虑。

sentences.en: When I was called and asked to do this, I paused, I thought, I wondered.
sentences.zh: 当我接到电话被要求做这件事时，我停顿了，我思考了，我疑惑了。

sentences.en: I took every precaution that I could.
sentences.zh: 我采取了所有我能采取的预防措施。

sentences.en: I asked every question that I could.
sentences.zh: 我提出了所有我能问的问题。

sentences.en: I waited until the weight of the entire nation's judicial system weighed in on it and told us it was legal.
sentences.zh: 我一直等到整个国家司法系统的分量对此做出评估，并告诉我们这是合法的。

sentences.en: I weighed that against the fact that they kept telling me every day a nuclear bomb was going to be exploded in the United States

sentences.en: and that because I told them to stop, I'd lost my nerve and it was going to be my fault if I didn't continue.
sentences.zh: 并且因为我叫他们停下来，我就是失去了勇气，如果我不继续下去，那就是我的错。

sentences.en: So I thought a great deal about it, sir.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此进行了深思熟虑，长官。

sentences.en: And I assume you would have, too, if you would have been in my place and stood up and gone to defend your nation.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你处在我的位置，站出来保卫国家，你也会这么做的。

sentences.en: It was an emotional time, Dor.
sentences.zh: 那是一个情绪激动的时期，多尔。

sentences.en: So don't interpret my emotionality as a personal affront.
sentences.zh: 所以请不要把我的情绪化当作是对个人的冒犯。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没有。

sentences.en: But these are serious questions you're asking.
sentences.zh: 但你问的这些都是严肃的问题。

sentences.en: It always feels like compensation helps clarify motivation.

sentences.zh: 总数达到了8100万美元，这是他们后来成立的咨询公司的费用，用来进行咨询并从中央情报局获得合同。

sentences.en: The United States government paid two psychologists $81 million to create and carry out this program.
sentences.zh: 美国政府向两名心理学家支付了8100万美元来制定和执行这个项目。

sentences.en: It is a lot of money.

sentences.en: They argue that they had to pay a lot of people, and so it sounds more than it is, but...
sentences.zh: 他们辩称，他们必须付钱给很多人，所以听起来比实际要多，但是……

sentences.en: $81 million, it seems, under any circumstances, is a lot of money.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Did these two doctors believe that the techniques they were using, did they ever believe that it caused pain?

sentences.en: Boy, this is, again, one of the really striking dichotomies here.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这又是这里真正引人注目的两极分化之一。

sentences.en: They go overboard, both Drs.

sentences.en: Do you think that people have suffered long-term harm as a result of that?

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: Maybe I need to tie you here for one hour so you can feel the pain, if you want to know the pain.
sentences.zh: 也许我需要把你绑在这里一个小时，这样你就能感受到痛苦了，如果你想知道痛苦是什么滋味的话。

sentences.en: We can take a break.

sentences.zh: 他在中情局的这些秘密监狱里经历了许多。

sentences.en: And who does he fault for this long-term impact?
sentences.zh: 他将这种长期影响归咎于谁？

sentences.en: He faults the people who held him and applied this to him, and he faults Drs.
sentences.zh: 他将责任归咎于囚禁他并对他实施这些手段的人，他还归咎于米切尔和杰森博士。

sentences.zh: 米切尔博士和杰森博士。

sentences.zh: 你认识一个叫詹姆斯·米切尔博士的人吗？

sentences.en: Even though they weren't actually the ones who worked with him.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们实际上并不是直接对他下手的人。

sentences.en: Do you know a man named Dr. Bruce Jessen?
sentences.zh: 你认识一个叫布鲁斯·杰森博士的人吗？

sentences.en: And that's one of their defenses.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们的辩护理由之一。

sentences.en: They say, we never met this man, and so why should we be held responsible for what he went through?
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们从未见过这个人，所以为什么我们要为他所遭受的苦难承担责任？

sentences.en: So you can see that those are two of the plaintiffs in this case?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出这是本案的两个原告？

sentences.zh: 我看到了这两个人。

sentences.zh: 如果你看一下增强型审讯技术（EITs）的清单，那基本上就是你的清单，对吧？

sentences.zh: 我不认为这是我的清单。

sentences.zh: 这是一份包含了我推荐给他们的技术的清单，但这是别人的清单。

sentences.en: Well, let's go through it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们逐一过一遍。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些项目不正是你清单上的那些项目吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: I mean, okay, sleep deprivation, that was on your list, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，好吧，睡眠剥夺，那在你的清单上，对吧？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I also remember being handicapped and naked in the room with no, any clothes on.
sentences.zh: 我还记得在房间里被戴上手铐且赤身裸体，身上没有任何衣服。

sentences.en: And then the next one is nudity.
sentences.zh: 接下来的一个是裸体。

sentences.en: That was on the list, right?
sentences.zh: 那在清单上，对吧？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember being tied on the wall.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己被绑在墙上。

sentences.en: Stress positions.
sentences.zh: 压力姿势。

sentences.en: That was on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 那在清单上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I remember being put in a box.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己被关在箱子里。

sentences.en: Cramped confinement.
sentences.zh: 狭小拘禁。

sentences.en: That was on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 那在清单上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Water is being poured on me.
sentences.zh: 水正浇在我身上。

sentences.en: Water dousing.
sentences.zh: 泼水。

sentences.en: That was on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 那在清单上。

sentences.en: No.

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Water dousing was not on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 泼水不在清单上。

sentences.zh: 你确定吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 非常确定。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Can't see me on the wall.
sentences.zh: 墙击看不见我。

sentences.en: Walling, that was on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 撞墙，那在清单上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 还有水刑，那在清单上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Herman Wilhelm Goethe.
sentences.zh: 赫尔曼·威廉·歌德。

sentences.en: It feels, Sherry, that a case like this is inevitably going to draw comparisons to these big moments in history where the world has asked for accountability after a traumatic
sentences.zh: 雪莉，感觉这样一个案件不可避免地会让人联想起历史上那些重大时刻，当时世界在经历了一场创伤性事件后要求追究责任

sentences.en: event, and it is individuals who are asked to be held accountable, not big governments, the classic case being the Nuremberg trials.
sentences.zh: 被要求追究责任的是个人，而不是庞大的政府，最经典的例子就是纽伦堡审判。

sentences.en: Does that feel apt?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这贴切吗？

sentences.en: Who do you want brought to justice?
sentences.zh: 你想把谁绳之以法？

sentences.en: If I could do anything on CIA, that's a separate issue.
sentences.zh: 如果我能对中情局做点什么，那是另一回事了。

sentences.en: The two doctors, why would they do that, such a thing?
sentences.zh: 那两位医生，他们为什么要做出这种事？

sentences.en: I think there's a larger sort of philosophical thing or a larger point to think about here, which is what is the role of the individual in a system when the system goes astray?
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有一个更大层面的哲学问题或更重大的观点需要思考，那就是当系统误入歧途时，个人在系统中的角色是什么？

sentences.en: And this is important for all of us to think about.
sentences.zh: 这对我们所有人来说都是一个重要的思考方向。

sentences.en: And I wrote for the New York Times about a really stressful situation inside a hospital
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》上写过关于一家医院内部一个极其紧张的局面的文章

sentences.en: after Hurricane Katrina, where doctors ultimately told me in my reporting that they intentionally
sentences.zh: 在卡特里娜飓风之后，医生们在我的报道中最终告诉我，他们故意

sentences.en: hastened patients' deaths by injecting them with drugs because they were so desperate and didn't know if they'd be rescued and became a criminal case around that.
sentences.zh: 通过注射药物加速了患者的死亡，因为他们太绝望了，不知道自己是否会被营救，并因此演变成了一起刑事案件。

sentences.en: And the question really boiled down to what is the responsibility of an individual within a whole system that fails?
sentences.zh: 核心问题归结为：在一个彻底失败的系统内部，个人的责任是什么？

sentences.en: And I think that may be the importance of a case like this, this idea that we were ordered to do this, we were in a system, and we followed orders.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能就是这样一个案件的重要性所在，这种观点认为我们是被命令这么做的，我们身处系统中，我们只是在服从命令。

sentences.en: So it'll be interesting to see what, if this case goes to trial, what is made of that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这个案件进入审判阶段，人们会对此做出何种反应，这将是非常有趣的。

sentences.en: And I'm not afraid, and I did my duty, and I stood up, and I went to war, and I'll stand up to any of them again.
sentences.zh: 我不害怕，我尽了我的职责，我挺身而出，我上了战场，我还会再次挺身面对他们任何人。

sentences.en: So why would I want to complicate my life more by going out in public when the public's already made up their mind about things?
sentences.zh: 既然公众已经对事情有了定论，我为什么还要出门在公众面前露面，给自己平添烦恼呢？
